title: Lumen Copilot WebSocket envelope
description: Transport framing for ALL WebSocket traffic (ADR-0003 §8, contracts/AGENTS.md). Every message is an envelope discriminated by `type`. Concrete product event payloads are slotted into `data` per `type`. Stream lifecycle: start -> (delta | event)* -> done | error, with exactly one terminal (done|error). The terminal is the last envelope that SETTLES the stream. One narrow exception (chat, #489): a terminal `done` MAY declare `data.pendingSuggestions=true`, in which case at most one `event:suggestions` envelope may still follow it within a bounded server-side grace window; the subscription holds open for that one post-terminal event and then closes. There is still exactly one terminal, it is still `done`, and nothing else may follow it. The chat feature's payloads (issue #37, CC-6 #24 / CC-11 #26) are defined under $defs and mapped by x-chatStream.

streamId.description: Correlates all messages of one logical stream (the chat send returns this as stream_id).

seq.description: Monotonically increasing per streamId; defines ordering.

data.description: Stream-open metadata; shape defined per feature (chat: ChatStartData).

Incremental output (e.g. a token chunk). Payload shape defined per feature (chat: ChatTokenDelta). Chunk boundaries are NOT semantic: the server may coalesce adjacent chunks into one delta (#487). Clients must concatenate in seq order and must not assume any relationship between delta count and provider tokens.

name.description: Structured side-band event name. Chat vocabulary: citation, tool_call, tool_result, code_output, code_result (the last two carry reusable sandbox output/outcome, ADR-0020 #457), step (live run-phase progress, spec 0006 #429), ask_user (the model's clarifying question, spec 0006 #429), suggestions (follow-up questions after the answer, spec 0006 #429), narration (a tool-calling turn's visible narration text, transient status — ADR-0016 §6 #414). Clients MUST ignore unknown names (forward compatibility).

data.description: Terminal success summary; shape defined per feature (chat: ChatDoneData). The terminal that settles the stream. Chat (#489) may set `data.pendingSuggestions=true` to signal that one post-terminal `event:suggestions` may still follow within a bounded grace window (see the root description); absent/false ⇒ the stream stops at this terminal.

problem.description: Same problem model as the REST error shape (openapi.yaml #/components/schemas/Problem).

messageId.description: Id the in-progress assistant message will be persisted under.

model.description: The REQUESTED model id (#413): the id the session/send chose. After a mid-answer failover the model that actually produced the answer may differ — done.model is authoritative for attribution.

ChatTokenDelta.description: `delta.data` — one streamed chunk of the assistant answer.

ChatCitation.description: `event.data` for name=citation. Mirrors openapi Citation (spec 0004 INV-3): a permitted passage the answer cites. The UI renders it as a clickable reference resolving to the document + span.

ChatToolCall.description: `event.data` for name=tool_call — the agent invoked a governed tool (CC-6 #24 / CC-7 #207). Surfaced so the UI can show 'searching…'. Every call is permission-filtered + allow-list-checked + audited via the tool registry (INV-2/INV-6).

tool.description: The registered tool name (CC-7 #207 — the tool set is open-ended). MVP retrieval tools: search_text = hybrid semantic+lexical passage search; search_documents = by filename/metadata; list_documents = enumerate the documents the user can access (no query); get_document = fetch a permitted document's text.

ChatToolResult.description: `event.data` for name=tool_result — outcome of a tool_call (CC-7 #207). A denied (off-allow-list / unapproved) or failing tool is reported as ok=false with a typed error, never a crashed stream.

tool.description: The registered tool name (CC-7 #207 — the tool set is open-ended).

ok.description: Whether the tool succeeded. Absent ⇒ treat as ok (back-compat). Additive (CC-7 #207).

error.description: Typed error code when ok=false (e.g. tool_not_permitted, approval_denied, tool_error, tool_timeout). Additive (CC-7 #207).

ChatDoneData.description: `done.data` — terminal success summary for a chat answer.

finishReason.description: e.g. stop, length, content_filter, ask_user (the turn ended with a clarifying question — spec 0006 #429).

model.description: The model that ACTUALLY produced this answer (#413, ADR-0016 §4): equals start.model unless a mid-answer failover switched to a tenant-configured fallback. Authoritative for attribution; additive (older servers omit it).

pendingSuggestions.description: When true (#489), the server will attempt follow-up suggestions AFTER this terminal and MAY deliver exactly one post-terminal `event:suggestions` within a bounded grace window; a subscriber must hold the subscription open for it and accept that one event without un-settling this terminal. Absent/false ⇒ the stream stops at this terminal (the default, and the case for a refusal/ask_user answer or when suggestions are disabled). Optimistic: `done.usage` covers the ANSWER only, and a suggestions attempt that fails/times out simply produces no event. Additive; older clients ignore it and close at the terminal as before.

cachedPromptTokens.description: Prompt tokens served from the provider's prompt cache this answer (#409, ADR-0016 §2.6). Additive; 0 when the provider reports no cache detail.

cacheWriteTokens.description: Prompt tokens written INTO the provider's prompt cache this answer (Anthropic-style cache creation). Additive; 0 when unreported.

ChatNarration.description: `event.data` for name=narration (ADR-0016 §6, #414): one chunk of a tool-calling turn's VISIBLE narration text, streamed live as transient status. Never a delta, never persisted (the streamed answer == stored message invariant is untouched); provider hidden-reasoning is excluded by construction. Additive: clients ignoring it lose nothing but liveness.

text.description: One or more narration chunks; append-ordered within the turn by seq. Adjacent chunks of the same turn may be coalesced server-side into a single envelope (#487), so chunk boundaries are not semantic — concatenate in seq order.

turn.description: The 1-based answer-loop turn this narration belongs to (clients reset the transient display per turn).

ChatStep.description: `event.data` for name=step — live run-phase progress (spec 0006 #429). Transient run-visibility state (ADR-0016 §6 posture): never persisted, absent after reload, replayed idempotently by seq. Keys fixed by spec 0006: prepare (context assembly), think (one model turn; `turn` ordinal), finalize (persist + citations), suggest (follow-up generation). Additive keys may appear later — clients render unknown keys generically off the server-supplied `label`. A re-`started` key restarts that step row (e.g. think per turn). Does NOT duplicate per-tool detail; tool_call/tool_result events carry that.

key.description: Stable machine key of the phase (spec 0006: prepare | think | finalize | suggest; open-ended).

label.description: Human-readable phase label to render (server-supplied; client never needs a key→label map).

state.description: Phase transition. A stream that errors may leave a step started — the terminal error supersedes it.

ChatAskUser.description: `event.data` for name=ask_user — the model asked the user a clarifying question instead of answering (spec 0006 #429). At most one per stream; the stream then ends with done(finishReason=ask_user) and NO suggestions event. The question is ALSO persisted on the assistant message (REST Message.question) so it stays answerable after reload; this event carries the same payload for live rendering. The user's choice is sent as an ordinary POST /chat/sessions/{id}/messages — there is no inbound WS path.

messageId.description: The assistant message the question persists under (same id as start.messageId).

question.description: The clarifying question text (also the persisted message content).

options.description: Mutually exclusive choices, rendered as clickable buttons; clicking sends the label as the next user message.

label.description: The choice text sent verbatim as the user's reply when clicked.

description.description: Optional one-line elaboration shown under the label.

allowFreeText.description: Whether typing a custom reply (the composer) is a sanctioned answer path (always true in practice; the composer is never disabled).

ChatSuggestions.description: `event.data` for name=suggestions — follow-up questions the user could ask next (spec 0006 #429). At most one per stream. Emitted OFF the answer's critical path (#489): the terminal `done` is published first (declaring `pendingSuggestions=true`), then this event arrives POST-terminal within a bounded grace window; absent when generation is disabled, failed, timed out, or the turn ended in ask_user. Transient (never persisted; gone after reload). Derived ONLY from the caller's own visible conversation — no retrieval, no new INV-2 surface.

messageId.description: The settled assistant message these follow-ups attach under.

suggestions.description: Short user-perspective questions, best first. The first is the composer's ghost-prefill candidate.

CodeOutput.description: `event.data` for name=code_output — one streamed chunk from a reusable sandbox run (ADR-0020). Emitted within the chat answer stream while `run_python` executes so the inspector can show stdout/stderr. `stream` identifies stdout or stderr; multiple events for a `runId` arrive in `seq` order. Non-terminal — one code_result carries the outcome.

runId.description: The code_runs.id this output belongs to (matches GET /code-runs/{codeRunId}).

callId.description: Correlates to the originating tool_call (ChatToolCall.callId) when the run was launched by a run_python tool call. Optional.

stream.description: Which output stream this chunk came from.

CodeResult.description: `event.data` for name=code_result — the terminal-ish outcome of a sandbox code run (ADR-0020). Exactly one arrives per `runId` after its code_output chunks, carrying the reusable sandbox id/generation, final status, exit code, duration, and emitted artifact ids. This is a run-level terminal event, NOT the chat stream's terminal — the chat stream still ends with its own done|error. The full record is inspectable via GET /code-runs/{runId}.

runId.description: The code_runs.id this result finalizes (matches GET /code-runs/{codeRunId}).

sandboxSessionId.description: Opaque reusable sandbox session used by this run; null when denied before allocation.

sandboxGeneration.description: Reusable sandbox generation used by this run; changes after reset or cancel.

callId.description: Correlates to the originating tool_call (ChatToolCall.callId) when applicable. Optional.

status.description: The run's terminal status (mirrors openapi CodeRunStatus, minus the non-terminal queued/running).

exitCode.description: Process exit code; null when killed/timeout/denied before producing one.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock execution time in milliseconds; null when the run never started (denied).

artifactIds.description: Ids of artifacts the run emitted (files collected + persisted via CC-B #208, tenant-scoped). Empty when the run produced none.

x-chatStream.description: Concrete payloads carried by a chat answer stream (issue #37). The transport envelope (root oneOf) is unchanged; these define what rides in `data` per `type`/`name`. When the agent runs code via run_python (ADR-0020 #457), sandbox output rides this same stream as event:code_output / event:code_result — additive, non-terminal for the chat stream itself.
x-chatStream.lifecycle: start(ChatStartData) -> ( delta(ChatTokenDelta) | event:step(ChatStep) | event:narration(ChatNarration) | event:tool_call(ChatToolCall) | event:tool_result(ChatToolResult) | event:citation(ChatCitation) | event:code_output(CodeOutput) | event:code_result(CodeResult) | event:ask_user(ChatAskUser) )* -> done(ChatDoneData) | error(Problem) -> [ event:suggestions(ChatSuggestions) ]?. Exactly one terminal (done|error). Constraints (spec 0006 #429 / #489): at most one ask_user per stream (then finishReason=ask_user, no suggestions); suggestions are OFF the critical path — the terminal done is published FIRST with data.pendingSuggestions=true, then at most one event:suggestions may follow POST-terminal within a bounded server grace window (derived from the suggestions timeout plus a small margin). The post-terminal event does not un-settle the terminal; nothing else may follow done, and a done without pendingSuggestions closes the stream immediately.
x-chatStream.codeRunSubStream: A run_python tool_call opens a code-run sub-sequence on the SAME chat stream, correlated by runId (and the originating tool_call's callId): zero or more event:code_output(CodeOutput) chunks in seq order, terminated by exactly one event:code_result(CodeResult) per runId. code_result is a run-level terminal, NOT the chat stream's terminal — the chat stream still ends with its own done|error. The full run record (code, stdout/stderr, resource_usage, sandbox generation) is inspectable at GET /code-runs/{runId}, tenant/owner-scoped (cross-tenant runId -> 404).
x-chatStream.subscribe: After POST /chat/sessions/{id}/messages returns { stream_id }, connect to GET /ws/chat/{stream_id}?access_token=<access JWT>. A browser WebSocket cannot set the Authorization header, so the access token rides the `access_token` query param. The stream is bound to its owner at send time; a missing/invalid token or a foreign/cross-tenant subscriber is denied identically (handshake rejected, no envelope emitted).
